title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures, Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page consolidates the canonical patterns, templates, and operating procedures used by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team to author SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, and site operating procedures. It also captures the top recurring support issues observed in the SDK/quickstart surface and canonical fixes to reduce repetitive triage.

Audience: DevEx engineers, technical writers, on-call support, and engineering teams producing public SDK/docs content.

Owner: DevEx (engineering). Primary point of contact: Ava Chen (devex@redwood.com).

Contents (quick nav)
- SDK guides checklist and template
- Quickstart templates (Python, JavaScript, Curl)
- API examples: canonical patterns and error-handling examples
- Docs site operating procedures: publishing, review, versioning, redirects, search indexing
- Top support issues and canonical fixes
- How to contribute / review process

1) SDK Guides: checklist & template\nShort intro: SDK guides should be concise, example-first, and include clear authentication patterns, error handling, and performance notes. Use the checklist below during PRs.

Checklist (use before merging any SDK guide):
- [ ] Has a one-paragraph summary explaining when to use the SDK vs direct API calls.
- [ ] Includes installation instructions for the primary package managers (pip/npm).
- [ ] Contains at least two runnable examples: a quickstart and an advanced example (batching, streaming, or function/tool calling).
- [ ] Shows authentication best-practice (API key env var, KMS/HSM note for Private deployments).
- [ ] Includes minimal error-handling and retry guidance for common transient errors (429, 5xx, network timeouts).
- [ ] Contains a short troubleshooting section with links to the top support issues.
- [ ] Has a test snippet (unit/integration) we can run in CI for docs smoke tests.
- [ ] Localized code snippets reviewed and linted.

SDK Guide Template (text to paste into a new page)
Title: <SDK> Quickstart
Summary: One-paragraph description.
Requirements: <language/runtime versions>, <package name/version>
Installation: 
- pip: pip install redwood-sdk
- npm: npm install @redwood/sdk
Authentication: 
1) Set REDWOOD_API_KEY environment variable (recommended):
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
2) For Private deployments: use REDWOOD_ENDPOINT and KMS config (link to secure-sdlc).
Quickstart (minimal runnable)
- Provide a 5–10 line example that demonstrates client creation and a single request (completion/chat/embedding).
Advanced example(s)
- Streaming responses example
- Batching example or efficient embeddings usage
Error handling & retries
- Example pseudo-code showing retry with exponential backoff for 429/5xx.
Performance notes
- When to use streaming vs batch, recommended timeouts, and concurrency limits.
Troubleshooting
- Link to top support issues.
References
- Link to API reference, SDK repo, release notes.

2) Quickstarts & templates (Python, JavaScript, curl)

Guidance: Quickstarts must run in <5 steps>. Prioritize copy/paste runnable snippets. Keep dependency footprint minimal. Include a single environment variable auth pattern.

Python quickstart (canonical)
1) pip install redwood-sdk
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
3) python -c "from redwood import Redwood; c=Redwood(); print(c.chat.create(\"Hello\"))"

JavaScript quickstart (canonical)
1) npm install @redwood/sdk
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
3) node -e "const {Redwood} = require('@redwood/sdk'); const c=new Redwood(); c.chat.create('Hello').then(console.log)"

cURL example (canonical)
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'

Templates to attach to new quickstart pages:
- Minimal runnable example (1–2 calls)
- Expandable "try it in your browser" snippet (if interactive playground exists)
- Security note snippet for Private customers
- Performance guidance snippet (timeouts, headers for streaming)

3) API examples: canonical patterns and error handling

Best practices:
- Always show the minimal request + the most common optional parameters.
- Include example responses (shortened) and explain fields like token_usage, latency_ms.
- Demonstrate both sync and streaming patterns where relevant.
- Provide a short table of common HTTP status codes, typical causes, and recommended actions.

Common response codes (table):
| Status | Typical cause | Action |
| 200 | Success | N/A |
| 401 | Invalid API key or expired token | Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, check key scope |
| 403 | Access denied (model or route) | Check customer plan, model entitlements |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded | Backoff + retry; consider Dedicated/reserved capacity |
| 500 | Server error | Retry with backoff; contact support if persistent |
| 503 | Capacity constrained or maintenance | Fallback to compatible model variant; region failover |

Example: retry pseudo-code (Python)
- Use exponential backoff (base=0.5s, factor=2, max=8s). Retry for 429 and idempotent 5xx. Avoid retrying non-idempotent operations without safeguards.

4) Docs site operating procedures (publishing & review)

Goal: Maintain high-quality, discoverable docs with consistent templates and fast turnaround for critical fixes.

Publishing checklist (PR author):
1) Link to this page in the PR description.
2) Confirm checklist items from the SDK guide section are satisfied.
3) Add labels: docs, sdk, quickstart, [language].
4) Verify code snippets run in docs smoke CI (we run minimal snippet tests).
5) Add release notes reference (if SDK or API change required).
6) Set page metadata (title, description, parent page).

Review process (owners):
- Technical review by DevEx engineer required (must include runtime test logs).
- Security review required if the page describes key management, private deployment networking, or admin APIs.
- Product/PM review for surface changes that affect billing or behaviour.

Versioning and redirects: 
- Use year-based filenames for major doc overhauls (e.g., sdk-quickstart-2026).
- Preserve old URLs with 301 redirects when content significantly changes. Create redirect tickets and link to them in the doc.

Search & tagging:
- Add language tags (python, javascript, curl) and feature tags (streaming, embeddings, function-calls).
- Ensure examples include alt-text and short snippets for search indexing.

Emergency doc rollback/patch flow:
1) If a public-facing bug is discovered, open an incident-linked docs PR with label docs-hotfix.
2) Assign on-call DevEx and a reviewer; target 2-hour SLA for critical fixes.
3) Add a temporary banner at the top of the impacted pages indicating workarounds.
4) After fix, remove banner and add postmortem note to related pages.

5) Top support issues and canonical fixes (Developer-facing)

Purpose: Provide a short triage playbook for oncall/support to reduce repeated escalations.

Issue 1: 401/Invalid API key errors
- Symptoms: Client receives 401 with message "invalid_api_key".
- Cause: Missing/rotated/misconfigured REDWOOD_API_KEY or using a private endpoint without REDWOOD_ENDPOINT.
- Canonical fix: Verify env var, verify key scope in console; for Private deployments ensure endpoint and TLS certs configured. Update quickstarts to always include test curl for auth verification.

Issue 2: 429 Rate limit / "Request rate too high"
- Symptoms: Clients see intermittent 429s at low concurrency.
- Cause: Misconfigured client-side parallelism, using very short timeouts, or user on free tier.
- Canonical fix: Add exponential backoff example in SDKs; include guidance to upgrade to Dedicated or use server-side batching. Update SDKs to expose helper retry policies.

Issue 3: Streaming responses drop or truncate
- Symptoms: Streaming connection closes with partial response.
- Cause: Client not consuming stream fast enough, reverse-proxy timeouts, or missing connection headers.
- Canonical fix: Document required headers, sample streaming client patterns for Node/Python, and recommended proxy timeout settings (keepalive >= 120s). Add a troubleshooting checklist to the streaming quickstart.

Issue 4: High cost / unexpected token usage
- Symptoms: Customers report higher-than-expected token billing.
- Cause: Long context windows, untrimmed messages, or using high-cost model variants.
- Canonical fix: Provide token accounting examples, add sample code for prefix/KV caching, and recommend quantized model profiles for embeddings. Include cost-estimate examples in quickstarts.

Issue 5: SDK compatibility / breaking changes after release
- Symptoms: Examples stop working after SDK or API minor version bump.
- Cause: Missing deprecation warnings, docs not updated, consumers pinning to older behavior.
- Canonical fix: Maintain a breaking-changes section in release notes, add compatibility table to SDK guides, and provide migration snippets. Run docs smoke tests against new SDK releases.

Issue 6: Incorrect or outdated code snippets in docs
- Symptoms: Snippets fail to run in customer environments.
- Cause: Docs drift, snippet linter not run, or environment mismatch.
- Canonical fix: Enforce snippet-linting and snippet-execution as part of PR CI; include language/version headers for all snippets.

Issue 7: Private deployment auth/network issues
- Symptoms: SDKs fail to connect to customer Private endpoint (timeout, cert errors).
- Cause: Misconfigured TLS, firewall rules, missing SNI, or incorrect REDWOOD_ENDPOINT.
- Canonical fix: Add a Private deployment quickstart that verifies certs (openssl s_client), required ports, and curl test commands. Provide a checklist for customers and SRE onboarding.

Issue 8: Embeddings mismatch across SDKs
- Symptoms: Embedding vectors differ in length or scale between client libraries.
- Cause: Different default preprocessors or model variant mismatches.
- Canonical fix: Standardize SDK defaults, document the embedding model & normalization, and add a cross-language test for embeddings consistency.

Issue 9: Long-tail platform errors (500/503) during peak
- Symptoms: Intermittent 500/503 affecting certain routes.
- Cause: Autoscaler lag, model warm-up, or kernel OOMs.
- Canonical fix: Recommend fallback-to-smaller-model policy in quickstarts, document retry windows, and include guidance to configure client-side graceful degradation.

Issue 10: Misunderstanding of streaming vs final-result semantics
- Symptoms: Customers expect streaming to return full structured output reliably on first chunk.
- Cause: Lack of clear examples and behavior descriptions.
- Canonical fix: Add explicit examples showing how to accumulate and parse streaming chunks and how to detect finalization.

6) How to contribute / review process

- Create a new page under /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates. Use the SDK Guide template at the top of this doc.
- Open a PR to the docs repo and link to this confluence page in the PR description.
- Assign a DevEx reviewer and include CI run logs for smoke snippet tests.
- If the change affects security, add security reviewer and set confidentiality to restricted until review completes.

Contact & escalation
- Primary: devex@redwood.com (Ava Chen).
- On-call: see /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks for current rotation.
- For customer-impacting doc regressions open a docs-hotfix incident and tag oncall SRE.
